schools.name: Arts & Letters
schools.blurb: Where the college learns to read, write and argue. Every other school will claim to teach these too.

programs.name: English
programs.blurb: The long conversation, with footnotes.

programs.name: History
programs.blurb: What happened, and who said so.

programs.name: Philosophy
programs.blurb: The questions, and a syllabus of people who failed to answer them.

programs.name: Fine Arts
programs.blurb: Studio work, critique, and a great deal of natural light.

programs.name: Music
programs.blurb: Theory, performance, and the acoustics of whatever hall is free.

schools.name: Science
schools.blurb: Laboratories, lectures, and the slow accumulation of things that are actually true.

programs.name: Biology
programs.blurb: Life, catalogued, dissected and occasionally escaped.

programs.name: Chemistry
programs.blurb: Matter, and what it does when provoked.

programs.name: Physics
programs.blurb: The universe, reduced to problems with answers in the back.

programs.name: Mathematics
programs.blurb: Proofs, and the chalk to write them with.

programs.name: Computer Science
programs.blurb: Machines that do what they are told, which is the problem.

schools.name: Engineering
schools.blurb: Things that must stand up, run, or fly, designed by people who will be blamed if they do not.

programs.name: Civil Engineering
programs.blurb: Bridges, roads and the buildings the college keeps losing to backlog.

programs.name: Mechanical Engineering
programs.blurb: Forces, machines, and the noise they make.

programs.name: Electrical Engineering
programs.blurb: Circuits, signals, and a building that smells faintly of solder.

programs.name: Chemical Engineering
programs.blurb: Chemistry, at a scale the fire marshal wants to hear about.

programs.name: Environmental Engineering
programs.blurb: Water, air, waste, and the stream at the edge of campus.

schools.name: Business
schools.blurb: Money, studied by people who intend to have some.

programs.name: Accounting
programs.blurb: The books, kept.

programs.name: Finance
programs.blurb: Money, over time, with risk.

programs.name: Marketing
programs.blurb: Why people buy things, and how to be there when they do.

programs.name: Management
programs.blurb: Getting other people to do the work, as a discipline.

programs.name: Economics
programs.blurb: Scarcity, choice, and graphs with two lines crossing.

schools.name: Health
schools.blurb: Clinics, wards and the people who will one day run them.

programs.name: Nursing
programs.blurb: The profession that is actually in the room.

programs.name: Public Health
programs.blurb: Health, at the scale of everyone.

programs.name: Pharmacy
programs.blurb: Medicines, and the small print.

programs.name: Physical Therapy
programs.blurb: Movement, restored.

programs.name: Nutrition
programs.blurb: Food, studied more carefully than the dining hall serves it.

schools.name: Law
schools.blurb: Rules, precedents, and the art of finding the exception.

programs.name: Legal Studies
programs.blurb: The law, before anyone is sued.

programs.name: Constitutional Law
programs.blurb: The founding documents, read very closely.

programs.name: Corporate Law
programs.blurb: Companies, and what they may and may not do.

programs.name: Criminal Law
programs.blurb: Crime, punishment, and the procedure in between.

programs.name: International Law
programs.blurb: Treaties, tribunals and a great many flags.

readings.schools: Schools founded of the six; each needs its own hall, a founding cost and, one day, a dean.
readings.programs: Programs open of the thirty; each costs money every year at its tier.
readings.programCosts: What the open programs cost to run this year: the programs line in the Treasury.
readings.halls: Open halls with no school in them yet: Founders Hall counts, and every Academic Hall.
readings.tier: Founded, Established or Renowned: the tier sets the seats, the courses on the catalogue, the cost and the quality ceiling.
readings.seats: How many students the program can teach at this tier before the classes crowd.
readings.annualCost: What this program costs to run each year at its tier.
readings.signatures: Signature programs named of the three allowed: cheaper to advance, and expected to stay advanced.
readings.crowding: Students enrolled against the seats every open program offers; over the seats, every program's quality is damped.
readings.advance: Advancing takes the money now, a senior hire of the next tier's rank assigned here, and the years; the works finish only with that hire still in place.
readings.lead: The senior hire the tier needs assigned: an Associate Professor to reach Established, a Professor to reach Renowned, and to stay there.
readings.neglect: Years running without its lead or under half its staff; two in a row and the tier drops.
